items.message: The `--corpus` path from `extra` is passed to `collect()` and then to `load_cases()` without any restriction on where it may point. An attacker who can supply a `--corpus` argument (or influence the value passed to it) can point it at any directory on disk — including outside the repository — and cause the trial to load and execute case files from that location. The immediate impact is arbitrary file read of any `.json` files reachable from the given path; if `load_cases` or `grade` deserialises…[truncated]

The `extra` path received from the CLI is used directly in `collect()` with only an `is_dir()` check before being handed to `load_cases()`. There is no check that `extra.resolve()` is within the working tree or any other trusted boundary. The same path-traversal concern as the CLI entry point: a caller supplying `../../` or an absolute path outside the project reaches arbitrary directories. The `is_dir()` guard prevents a missing-path error but does not constrain where the path may point.

When `--record` is set, the code calls `credentials_for(auth, selected.provider)` and builds a `RecordingProvider`. The model string passed via `--model` is taken from user input and used unsanitised to select a provider and construct a `Model` object. If `Model()` or `registry.provider_for()` uses the string to look up or construct a network endpoint, a malformed or adversarially chosen model string could redirect recording traffic. In `_review_case`, the `diff` string extracted from `case.input` is placed directly into a `Review` request that is passed to `adapter.invoke`. The source of `diff` is a case file loaded from disk (pack corpus or `--corpus` path). If a crafted corpus file contains a `diff` value designed to exploit downstream prompt handling — for instance, injecting reviewer instructions — it reaches the prompt construction layer without sanitisation.
